q: What is the earliest age at which you can apply for a Georgia Class CP instructional permit?
b: 15 and a half
exp: Georgia accepts a Class CP application on or after your 15th birthday.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 2, Class C Instructional Permit, p. 8

q: How many questions are on the road signs part of the Georgia knowledge exam?
exp: The road signs part has 20 questions, and so does the road rules part.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: How many correct answers do you need to pass each part of the Georgia knowledge exam?
b: 14 out of 20
c: 16 out of 20
d: 12 out of 20
exp: Each part has 20 questions, and you must answer at least 15 correctly on each one.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: Who may supervise a driver holding a Georgia Class CP permit?
a: Any licensed driver at least 18, seated anywhere in the car
b: A licensed driver at least 18, seated beside the driver
c: A licensed driver at least 25, seated in the back seat
d: A licensed Class C driver at least 21, seated beside the driver
exp: The supervisor must be at least 21, licensed for a Class C vehicle, able to take control and in the seat next to you.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 2, Conditions of a Class CP, p. 8

q: How long must you hold a Georgia instructional permit before you can apply for a Class D license?
b: One year and one day
c: Nine months and one day
d: Two years and one day
exp: You must be at least 16 and have held the permit for one year and one day.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 2, Class D Provisional License, p. 8

q: During which hours may a Georgia Class D license holder not drive at all?
b: 1 a.m. to 6 a.m.
c: Midnight to 5 a.m.
d: 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.
exp: Class D drivers may not drive from 12:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m., and there are no exceptions.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 6, Conditions of a Class D, p. 27

q: During the first six months on a Georgia Class D license, who may ride with you?
a: Only members of your immediate family
b: One friend under 21 and your family
c: Up to three friends under 21
d: Anyone, as long as a parent is also in the car
exp: For the first six months, only immediate family members may be passengers.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 6, Conditions of a Class D, p. 27

q: How much supervised driving must a Georgia teen complete before the Class D road test?
a: At least 40 hours, including 10 at night
b: At least 50 hours, including 10 at night
c: At least 40 hours, including 6 at night
d: At least 30 hours, including 6 at night
exp: A teen needs at least 40 hours of driving experience, 6 of them at night, certified by an affidavit at the road test.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 6, Driver Education Requirements, p. 27

q: Under Joshua's Law, how many hours of classroom or online instruction must a 16 or 17 year old complete?
exp: An approved course includes 30 hours of classroom or certified online instruction.
src: DDS Joshua's Law Requirements (dds.georgia.gov/node/3571)

q: A Georgia driver under 18 collects 4 points within 12 months. What happens?
a: The driver gets a warning letter only
b: The license is suspended
c: Nothing until the driver reaches 15 points
d: The driver must retake the knowledge exam
exp: Drivers under 18 are suspended for 4 or more points in any 12 month period.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 10, The Points System, p. 49

q: In which language is the road signs part of the Georgia knowledge exam given?
b: Any language DDS offers for road rules
c: English only
d: English, with an audio translation on request
exp: Road signs and the driving test are given in English only; the road rules part is offered in some other languages.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: You fail the road rules part of the knowledge exam for the first time. When may you retake it?
b: After 30 days
c: The next day
d: After 14 days
exp: After a first failure, you wait until the next day to retake the part you failed.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: You fail the same part of the Georgia knowledge exam a second time. How long must you wait?
b: 7 days
c: 30 days
d: 3 days
exp: After a second or later failure, you must wait 7 days before retaking that part.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: When is the $10 Class CP permit fee paid?
b: Only if you fail the first time
c: When you receive your Class D license
d: Before each attempt at the knowledge exam
exp: The fee is paid before testing, is not refunded if you fail, and must be paid again before every attempt.
src: DDS fees page (dds.georgia.gov/node/726)

q: For how long is a Georgia Class CP permit valid?
b: 5 years
c: Until your 18th birthday
d: Up to 2 years
exp: Class C instructional permits are valid for up to two years.
src: DDS online manual, Section 2 (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33606)

q: What is the minimum vision standard for a Georgia car license?
b: 20/40 in both eyes, without glasses
c: 20/100 in one eye, glasses allowed
d: 20/20 in one eye, without glasses
exp: Georgia requires 20/60 in one eye, with or without corrective lenses, and a 140 degree field of vision.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 1, Vision Requirements, p. 4

q: What does ADAP stand for in Georgia teen licensing?
b: Alcohol and Drug Awareness Program
c: Accident and Danger Avoidance Plan
d: Approved Driver Apprentice Permit
exp: Applicants under 18 must complete the Alcohol and Drug Awareness Program, taught in most schools and online.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 2, Applicants under age 18, p. 4

q: During the second six months on a Georgia Class D license, how many passengers under 21 who are not immediate family may ride with you?
b: Two
c: One
d: Three
exp: In the second six months, one non-family passenger under 21 is allowed.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 6, Conditions of a Class D, p. 27

q: After your first 12 months on a Georgia Class D license, how many passengers under 21 who are not immediate family may ride with you?
b: Up to two
c: Any number
d: Up to three
exp: After the first two six-month periods, up to three non-family passengers under 21 may ride with you.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 6, Conditions of a Class D, p. 27

q: For the Georgia Class D passenger limits, who counts as immediate family?
a: Your household plus parents, siblings, grandparents
b: Your parents and guardians, but not siblings
c: Any relative, including cousins who live elsewhere
d: Any relative or family friend over 21
exp: Immediate family includes parents, stepparents, grandparents, siblings, stepsiblings, children and anyone living at your residence.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 6, Conditions of a Class D, p. 27

q: You hold a Georgia Class D license and your shift ends at 12:30 a.m. May you drive home?
a: Yes, driving home from work is an exception
b: Yes, if you carry a note from your employer
c: Yes, if a parent signed a work permission form
d: No, the midnight to 5 a.m. ban has no exceptions
exp: The Class D night ban has no exceptions for work, school or any other reason.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 6, Conditions of a Class D, p. 27

q: What must a Georgia Class D holder have to move up to a Class C license at 18?
a: A new road test with an examiner
b: No major traffic convictions for 12 months
c: 40 more hours of supervised driving
d: A passing score on a new knowledge exam
exp: At 18, a Class D holder with no major traffic convictions in the prior 12 months can get a Class C without new tests.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 2, Exchanging a Class D license, p. 9

q: Who must ride along during a Georgia virtual road test?
b: Nobody; the car must be empty except for you
c: A DDS examiner in the passenger seat
d: A licensed friend 18 or older
exp: In a virtual test, the examiner watches remotely, and a licensed parent, guardian or other adult 21 or older rides as a passenger.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: How soon must a new Georgia resident apply for a Georgia license to keep driving?
b: Within 90 days
c: Within one year
d: Within 30 days
exp: Georgia law requires new residents to get a Georgia license or permit within 30 days.
src: DDS online manual, Section 2 (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33606)

q: An 18 year old new resident has a valid license from another U.S. state. Which test is required for a Georgia license?
a: The knowledge exam and a vision test
b: A vision test only
c: The road test only
d: All three tests
exp: A valid out-of-state license transfers after you surrender it, show your documents and pass a vision test.
src: DDS online manual, Section 2 (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33606)

q: A new Georgia resident holds a license from a country with no reciprocity agreement. What must they pass?
a: All three: vision, knowledge and road
b: The vision test and knowledge exam
c: The vision test and road test
d: The knowledge exam and road test
exp: Licenses from countries without an agreement do not transfer, so all three tests are required.
src: DDS Drivers From Other Nations (dds.georgia.gov/node/2301)

q: Drivers from which country can trade in an equivalent car license in Georgia with only a vision test?
b: Mexico
c: Brazil
d: India
exp: Georgia has reciprocity with South Korea and Taiwan, among others on the DDS list; a vision test is still required.
src: DDS Drivers From Other Nations (dds.georgia.gov/node/2301)

q: A 20 year old applies for a first Georgia license without getting a permit first. What must they sign besides passing the tests?
b: An affidavit of 40 supervised hours
c: A school enrollment form (DS-1)
d: An ADAP completion certificate
exp: Adults applying directly for Class C must affirm 40 hours of supervised driving, including 6 at night.
src: DDS online manual, Section 2 (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33606)

q: A 19 year old Georgia driver is convicted of reckless driving for the first time. What happens to the license?
b: It is suspended for 12 months
c: Points are added, but no suspension
d: It is suspended for 6 months
exp: Under 21, a first conviction for reckless driving or any 4-point offense brings a 6 month suspension.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-5-57.1; GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 6, p. 27

q: Who can ask DDS to cancel a Georgia teen's permit or license before the teen turns 18?
b: A police officer after any traffic stop
c: The teen's driving instructor
d: The adult who signed the application
exp: The parent, guardian or responsible adult who signed may request revocation at any time before the 18th birthday.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 6, Revocation of Minor's License, p. 27

q: Which document usually proves school status for a Georgia applicant under 18?
a: A school enrollment form, the DS-1
b: Last year's final report card
c: A student ID card with a photo
d: A letter from your school counselor
exp: Teens bring a DS-1 from school, dated within 30 days, or another listed document such as a diploma or GED.
src: georgia.gov Class CP page (georgia.gov/node/25001); GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 6, p. 26

q: Where do you take the official Georgia knowledge exam for a permit?
a: Online at home, with a parent watching
b: In person at a DDS Customer Service Center
c: At your high school, with a teacher
d: By mail, with a signed form
exp: DDS offers a free practice test online, but the exam itself is taken in person at a Customer Service Center.
src: georgia.gov/node/25001; DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: Under Joshua's Law, what may replace 6 hours of driving with a certified instructor?
a: 10 more hours of online classroom study
b: A second ADAP course and a parent signature
c: The Parent/Teen Driving Guide, done with a parent
d: 6 more hours of supervised night driving
exp: The behind-the-wheel part can be done with a certified instructor or through the parent-taught Parent/Teen Driving Guide.
src: DDS Joshua's Law Requirements (dds.georgia.gov/node/3571)

q: How late may you start the knowledge exam at a Georgia Customer Service Center?
b: At least 30 minutes before closing
c: At least 2 hours before closing
d: Before noon on weekdays
exp: DDS requires you to begin the exam at least 30 minutes before the center closes.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: Under 21, speeding by how much is a 4-point offense that suspends a Georgia license?
b: 15 mph or more over
c: 24 mph or more over
d: 20 mph or more over
exp: Speeding 24 to 33 mph over the limit is a 4-point offense (34 or more is 6 points). Any offense worth 4 or more points suspends a driver under 21.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 10, Types of Suspensions, p. 46

q: If you need glasses to pass the Georgia vision test, what happens?
a: You must take a road test every year
b: You may drive in daylight hours only
c: Your license gets a lenses restriction
d: You must pass a road test each renewal
exp: Passing only with glasses or contacts places a corrective lenses restriction on your license.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 1, Vision Requirements, p. 5

q: What do you get on the day you pass your Georgia Class D road test?
a: The plastic card, printed on the spot
b: A temporary license; the card comes by mail
c: Nothing until a parent signs a second form
d: A permit good for 30 days of supervised driving
exp: After you pass, DDS issues a temporary license and mails the permanent one.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: Which is true about a 17 year old in Georgia who has not taken driver education?
a: They still cannot get a Class D without it
b: They may get a Class D with 60 supervised hours instead
c: They may get a Class C right away
d: They need just ADAP and 40 hours
exp: Since Joshua's Law covers both 16 and 17 year olds, a 17 year old needs driver education for a Class D (enlisted military teens are the exception).
src: DDS Joshua's Law Requirements (dds.georgia.gov/node/3571)

q: In Georgia, what is the fine range for speeding in a marked highway work zone?
c: Double the normal fine, with no set range
exp: Georgia treats work zone speeding as a serious misdemeanor with a fine of $100 to $2,000, up to 12 months in jail, or both.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-188(e); GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, p. 22

q: When a Georgia work zone speed limit is at least 10 mph lower than normal, how far before it must a Reduced Speed Ahead sign stand?
b: At least 100 feet
c: At least 200 feet
d: At least one mile
exp: Georgia law requires a Reduced Speed Ahead sign at least 600 feet before such a reduced speed zone.

q: How far ahead of a school or school crossing does Georgia place the five-sided school sign?
b: 150 to 700 feet
d: Right at the crosswalk
exp: The pentagon school sign stands not less than 150 feet nor more than 700 feet before the school grounds or crossing.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Shapes of Signs, p. 28

q: In Georgia, work zone speeding penalties apply when which of these is present along with the work zone signs?
a: Workers or hazards such as barriers
b: A police car with lights flashing
c: A posted speed camera sign
d: A detour sign at the next exit
exp: Georgia's higher penalties apply when workers are present or hazards such as barriers, work vehicles or drop-offs are there.

q: In a Georgia work zone, a slow vehicle with flashing amber lights is working in the road. What must you do?
a: Slow down and yield the right of way to it
b: Pass it quickly on the shoulder
c: Flash your headlights so it moves over
d: Stop and wait until the work is finished
exp: Georgia drivers must yield to work vehicles showing amber lights and follow their directions.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Yield to Amber Lights, p. 22

q: When does the lower limit on a Georgia School Speed Limit sign with flashing lights apply?
a: All day on every day of the school year
b: Whenever children can be seen nearby
c: When a crossing guard is on duty
d: While lights flash or during posted hours
exp: The reduced school speed limit is in effect when the yellow lights are flashing or during the posted times.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Regulatory Signs, p. 29

q: How does a Georgia school zone speed camera ticket reach the driver?
a: A civil ticket is mailed to the car's owner
b: An officer must stop the car on the spot
c: It is added to your record as points right away
d: It is sent to the school, not the owner
exp: School zone cameras issue civil penalties to the registered owner by mail.

q: You stop at a red octagon sign. There is no stop line and no crosswalk. Where should you stop?
a: Right next to the sign post itself
b: Where you can best see cross traffic
c: Inside the intersection, at its edge
d: One full car length before the sign
exp: With no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the point where you have the best view of oncoming traffic.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Shapes of Signs, p. 28

q: A red and white triangle points down at your road. What does it require?
a: Stop every time, even when the road is clear
b: Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
c: Slow, stop if needed, and let traffic go
d: Keep going; other traffic must yield to you
exp: A yield sign means slow to a safe speed, stop if necessary and give the right of way to traffic already there or close.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Shapes of Signs, p. 28

q: What does a round yellow sign beside the road warn you about?
b: A railroad crossing ahead
c: A roundabout ahead
d: A hospital zone ahead
exp: The round sign stands a few hundred feet before a railroad crossing; slow down, look and listen.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Shapes of Signs, p. 28

q: A white vertical rectangle is posted beside the road. What kind of sign is it usually?
b: A warning about a road hazard
c: A regulatory sign you must obey
d: A sign for a nearby gas station
exp: Vertical rectangles are generally regulatory signs, which tell you what you must do.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Shapes of Signs, p. 28

q: What do horizontal rectangle signs usually show?
b: Speed limits, turn bans and other rules
c: Hazards such as curves or hills
d: Railroad crossings and school zones
exp: Horizontal rectangles are generally guide signs showing places, directions or other information.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Shapes of Signs, p. 28

q: On a regulatory sign, what does a red circle with a red slash across a symbol mean?
b: The action shown is allowed only at night
c: A hazard is ahead
d: The action shown is not allowed
exp: A red circle with a slash from upper left to lower right means no; the symbol shows what is prohibited.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Regulatory Signs, p. 29

q: A white sign shows a black arrow bent into a U, inside a red circle with a red slash. What does it mean?
a: A U-turn lane begins just ahead
b: No U-turns at this intersection
c: The road curves sharply ahead
d: U-turns are allowed only on green
exp: This sign means you cannot turn around to go back the other way at this intersection.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Regulatory Signs, p. 29

q: A sign reads REDUCED SPEED AHEAD. What does it tell you?
a: The speed limit has just ended
b: Slow traffic must use the left lane
c: A lower speed limit begins shortly
d: Speed cameras are ahead
exp: This sign warns that you are approaching an area with a reduced speed limit, so start slowing.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Regulatory Signs, p. 29

q: On a road with two lanes going your way, a sign reads SLOWER TRAFFIC KEEP RIGHT. What does it mean?
a: Trucks must use the right lane only
b: The right lane ends soon; merge left
c: Slower drivers should use the right lane
d: Everyone must stay right except in an emergency
exp: When two or more lanes go your way, slower traffic should travel in the right lane.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Regulatory Signs, p. 29

q: A white sign shows a black arrow curving to the right around a raised island. What must you do?
a: Turn right at the next street
b: Pass the vehicle ahead on the right
c: Keep to the right of the median or obstruction
d: Merge into the right lane, which is ending
exp: The Keep Right sign means traffic must keep to the right of a median or obstruction.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Regulatory Signs, p. 29

q: At a red light, you see a sign reading NO TURN ON RED. You want to turn right. What should you do?
a: Turn right after a full stop
b: Turn right if no one is coming
c: Turn right only if a pedestrian waves you on
d: Wait for the green light before turning
exp: This sign forbids a right turn on red even after a complete stop.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Regulatory Signs, p. 29

q: A black rectangle shows a white arrow with the words ONE WAY. What does it mean?
a: Traffic may travel only in the direction of the arrow
b: The road narrows to one lane
c: You must turn in the direction of the arrow now
d: Only one car at a time may pass
exp: A One Way sign means you may travel only in the direction the arrow points.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Regulatory Signs, p. 29; MUTCD One Way sign R6-1

q: A yellow sign warns of a low underpass and shows a height. When must you not go under it?
a: When your vehicle or load is taller
b: Only when you are driving a truck
c: When the height shown is under 14 feet
d: When your vehicle is within a foot of it
exp: Do not enter if your vehicle or its cargo is taller than the clearance shown.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 30

q: A yellow diamond reads DIP. What should you do?
a: Speed up to climb the next hill
b: Slow down; the road drops ahead
c: Change lanes to avoid a bump
d: Stop and check for water in it
exp: A Dip sign warns of a low spot in the road ahead, so slow down.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 30

q: A yellow diamond shows a truck on a steep slope. What is the safest response?
a: Slow down and use a lower gear
b: Speed up to keep your momentum
c: Shift into neutral to save fuel
d: Ride the brakes all the way down
exp: A steep hill sign means slow down and shift to a lower gear to control speed and protect the brakes.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 30

q: A yellow diamond shows a T shape: your road ends at a cross road. What should you do?
a: Keep going straight across the road
b: Slow, and be ready to yield or stop
c: Speed up to turn before cross traffic arrives
d: Turn right without slowing or stopping
exp: The road you are on ends ahead, so prepare to yield or stop and turn one way or the other.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 30

q: A yellow diamond shows a car with wavy skid marks. According to the Georgia manual, when is that road most dangerous?
a: After it has rained for several hours
b: In the first half hour of rain
c: After the rain stops and it dries
d: At night when the road is dry
exp: Oil and grime mix with the first rain, so the first half hour of rainfall is the most hazardous.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 31

q: A yellow diamond shows a red octagon and an arrow. What is ahead?
b: A divided highway begins
c: A stop sign; begin slowing now
d: A school bus stop ahead
exp: This warning sign tells you there is a stop sign ahead, so slow down and be ready to stop.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 31

q: A yellow diamond shows a red and white triangle with an arrow. What is ahead?
a: A stop sign; prepare to stop completely
b: A no-passing zone; stay in your lane
c: A merge; adjust speed to let traffic in
d: A yield sign; slow and be ready to stop
exp: The Yield Ahead sign warns that a yield sign is coming; slow and be prepared to stop.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 31

q: A sign shows a person walking at a crosswalk. A pedestrian is in the crosswalk. What must you do?
a: Stop and wait until the pedestrian is out of your path
b: Slow down and pass behind the pedestrian with care
c: Go once they pass the center of your lane
d: Stop if a crossing guard is there to signal
exp: Drivers must stop and remain stopped while pedestrians are in the crosswalk.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 31

q: A yellow pennant on the left side of the road marks the start of a no passing zone. When must your pass be finished?
b: Before the next solid white line
c: Before the next intersection, wherever it is
d: Before you reach the sign
exp: Any passing must be completed before you reach the No Passing Zone sign.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 31

q: A yellow plaque reading 35 MPH is mounted under a curve warning sign. What does it give?
a: The new speed limit for the rest of the road
b: A safe advisory speed for that curve
c: The minimum speed for the curve
d: The speed limit for trucks only
exp: Advisory speed plaques show the speed at which you should take the hazard; usually it is below the posted limit.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 31; Section 8, Curves, p. 38

q: On a Georgia highway, where do milepost numbers start at zero?
a: At the north or east border
b: At the state capitol in Atlanta
c: At the south or west border
d: At the nearest county line
exp: Mileposts count from zero at the south or west end of the route.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Guide Signs, p. 32

q: An orange triangle with a red border is on the back of a farm vehicle. What does it tell you?
b: The vehicle is about to turn left
c: The vehicle moves slower than 25 mph
d: The vehicle is an emergency vehicle
exp: The slow-moving vehicle emblem marks a vehicle traveling under 25 mph.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Guide Signs, p. 32

q: A crossbuck has a small sign below it showing the number 2. What does the number mean?
b: Stop 2 car lengths from the tracks
c: The crossing is 2 miles ahead
d: There are two sets of tracks to cross
exp: A sign below the crossbuck shows the number of tracks, so look for a second train.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Guide Signs, p. 32

q: A green rectangle with a white bicycle symbol and the word ROUTE is beside the road. What does it mark?
a: A road where bicycles are banned
b: A bike parking area ahead
c: A lane only for bicycles at all times
d: An official bicycle route; watch for riders
exp: This sign marks an officially designated bicycle route, so expect cyclists.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Guide Signs, p. 32

q: A yellow diamond reads NARROW BRIDGE. What does the Georgia manual say it means?
a: The bridge is closed to wide trucks
b: It is narrower than the road, with two lanes
c: The bridge has a weight limit for trucks
d: The bridge is one lane only, so take turns
exp: The bridge ahead is narrower than the road and allows only two lanes of traffic, so slow down and keep right.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 30

q: A yellow diamond reads SOFT SHOULDER. When may you drive on that shoulder?
b: Only to pass a slow car
c: Only in an emergency
d: Any time at low speed
exp: A soft shoulder may not hold your car; use it only in emergencies.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 30

q: A yellow diamond shows a traffic light with three lamps. What should you do?
a: Stop; the signal ahead is broken
b: Speed up to make the green light
c: Change lanes; the signal controls only one lane
d: Slow down; a traffic signal is ahead
exp: This sign warns of traffic signals at the intersection ahead, so slow down and be ready to stop.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 31

q: A yellow diamond shows a straight arrow with a second lane joining it from the right. What should you do?
a: Speed up so merging cars must wait
b: Be ready to let merging traffic in safely
c: Move onto the shoulder to let them in
d: Stop and let every merging car go first
exp: Traffic is merging from the right; adjust your speed and position so it can merge safely.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 31

q: A yellow diamond shows two arrows separated by a rounded island, as a median begins. What is ahead?
b: A one-way street ends
c: A traffic circle ahead
d: A divided highway begins
exp: The Divided Highway sign tells you a median is starting; prepare to keep right of it.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Warning Signs, p. 30

q: What color are Georgia's signs that point to gas, food, lodging and hospitals?
b: Green with white letters
c: Brown with white letters
d: Yellow with black letters
exp: Service signs along Georgia highways are blue and white.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Service Signs, p. 33

q: What color are warning signs for construction and maintenance work in Georgia?
b: White with black markings
c: Orange with black markings
d: Red with white markings
exp: Construction and maintenance warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Construction and Maintenance Warning Signs, p. 33

q: In Georgia, when may you turn left on a steady red light?
a: From any street onto a one-way street, after stopping
b: From any street, if no traffic is coming
c: From a one-way street onto a one-way street, after stopping
d: From a two-way street onto a two-way street, after stopping
exp: Georgia allows left on red only from a one-way street onto a one-way street, from the left lane, after a full stop.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-21(a)(3)(D); GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, p. 18

q: You face a steady red arrow pointing right at a Georgia intersection. May you turn right after stopping?
a: Yes, after a full stop, unless a sign forbids it
b: No; wait until the arrow changes
c: Yes, if no pedestrians are present
d: Yes, but only with a flashing yellow arrow beside it
exp: Georgia law says traffic facing a steady red arrow may not enter the intersection to make the arrow's movement.

q: You want to turn right on a steady red light in Georgia, and no sign forbids it. What comes first?
a: A rolling stop if the road looks clear
b: A tap of the horn to warn pedestrians
c: Waiting for the pedestrian signal to show WALK
d: A full stop, then yield to cars and people
exp: Right on red is allowed only after a complete stop and after yielding to all traffic and pedestrians.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-21(a)(3)(B); GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, pp. 17 to 18

q: You are on a two-way street and want to turn left onto a one-way street at a red light in Georgia. What should you do?
b: Turn after a full stop from the left lane
c: Turn without stopping if clear
d: Turn after a full stop from the center lane
exp: Left on red is allowed only when both streets are one-way; from a two-way street you must wait for green.

q: On a Georgia four-lane road with no median, a school bus stops with red lights flashing. Who must stop?
b: Traffic in both directions
c: Only traffic in the lane next to the bus
d: Only traffic coming toward the bus
exp: Georgia requires traffic from either direction to stop unless the roadways are separated by a grass median, unpaved area or barrier.

q: In Georgia, what is the most you can be fined for failing to move over or slow down for a stopped emergency vehicle?
exp: Violating the Move Over law for emergency vehicles carries a fine of up to $500.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-16; GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, p. 18

q: In Georgia, how close may you follow a fire truck answering an alarm?
b: No closer than 500 feet
c: Any distance, if you keep pace
d: No closer than 200 feet
exp: Georgia drivers may not follow fire apparatus or other emergency vehicles on a call closer than 200 feet.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Following Emergency Vehicles, p. 24

q: On a Georgia highway divided by a grass median, a school bus on the other side stops with red lights flashing. What must you do?
a: Proceed with care; you need not stop
b: Stop until the bus moves
c: Stop, then go when the driver waves
d: Slow to 10 mph until you pass it
exp: Traffic on the opposite roadway of a highway split by a grass median, unpaved area or barrier is not required to stop.

q: A Georgia road has two lanes each way and a paved center turn lane. A school bus stops with red lights flashing. Who must stop?
b: Only traffic in the turn lane
c: No one, because of the turn lane
d: Traffic in both directions
exp: A paved turn lane is not a grass median, unpaved area or barrier, so traffic both ways must stop.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-163(b); DDS school bus guidance

q: What is the minimum fine for illegally passing a stopped school bus in Georgia?
exp: Passing a stopped school bus is punished as a high and aggravated misdemeanor with a fine of at least $1,000.

q: How many points does illegally passing a stopped school bus add to a Georgia driving record?
exp: Unlawfully passing a school bus is a 6-point offense.

q: In Georgia, when may you move again after stopping for a school bus?
a: When the bus moves or turns off its flashing signals
b: After 30 seconds
c: When the stop arm starts to fold, even if lights still flash
d: As soon as the children reach the curb
exp: Stay stopped until the bus resumes motion or its signals are off, and watch for children still crossing.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-163(a); GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 9, p. 44

q: Under Georgia's Move Over law, a tow truck with flashing amber lights is stopped on the shoulder and you cannot change lanes. What must you do?
a: Keep your speed and stay in your lane
b: Slow below the speed limit and be ready to stop
c: Stop in your lane until the tow truck leaves
d: Drive on the far shoulder to pass
exp: If a lane change is unsafe, slow to a speed below the posted limit and be prepared to stop.

q: An ambulance with a siren and flashing lights comes up behind you in Georgia. Where should you go?
a: To the left edge or median, and stop there
b: Stop right where you are, even in the intersection
c: To the right edge, clear of the intersection, and stop
d: To the right edge, then keep moving slowly
exp: Georgia law requires drivers to pull to the right-hand edge or curb, clear of any intersection, and stop until it passes.

q: In Georgia, how close may you park to a fire truck stopped to answer a fire alarm?
b: No closer than 200 feet
c: No closer than 500 feet
d: Anywhere it is legal to park
exp: Georgia drivers may not park within 500 feet of fire apparatus stopped at an alarm.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Following Emergency Vehicles, p. 24

q: Which stopped vehicles does Georgia's Move Over law protect with a fine of up to $250?
a: Any private car stopped on the shoulder with hazards on
b: Tow, maintenance and utility trucks with cones or amber lights
c: School buses stopped to load or unload children
d: Parked police cars on the shoulder with no lights on
exp: The law covers tow, recovery, maintenance and utility vehicles with cones or flashing yellow, amber or white lights, with fines up to $250.

q: In Georgia, how far before your left turn may you enter a shared center turn lane?
b: No more than 300 feet
c: No more than 500 feet
d: Up to a quarter mile
exp: Georgia law allows the center turn lane only for left turns, entered no more than 300 feet before the turn.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Turn Lanes, p. 37

q: In Georgia, a driver behind you wants to pass. Is it legal to flash your left turn signal to tell them it is safe?
a: No, it is against Georgia law
b: Yes, it is the proper courtesy signal
c: Yes, on a two-lane road
d: Yes, if you also wave your hand
exp: Georgia law forbids flashing turn signals as a courtesy or do pass signal to drivers behind you.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Illegal Signals, p. 19

q: Where does the Georgia manual say you must never make a U-turn?
a: On any street with a center line
b: Anywhere in a business district
c: On a curve or near the top of a hill
d: At any intersection with a traffic light
exp: Do not make a U-turn on a curve or near a hilltop where drivers from either direction cannot see you, or where signs forbid it.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, U-Turns, p. 20

q: How long must you signal before a turn under Georgia law?
a: For at least 100 feet before the turn
b: For at least 3 seconds before the turn
c: Briefly, then cancel it before you turn
d: Continuously, early enough to warn others
exp: Georgia sets no fixed distance; the signal must be appropriate, timely and continuous enough to warn traffic.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-123; GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Turn Signals, p. 19

q: Your car's turn signals stop working right before your Georgia road test. What must you be able to do?
a: Pass the test using hand signals
b: Skip all turns on the route
c: Use your hazard flashers for turns
d: Nothing; the test is canceled
exp: If the test vehicle has no working turn signals, you must be able to pass using hand signals.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: What is Georgia's speed limit in an urban or residential district when no sign is posted?
b: 30 mph
c: 35 mph
d: 40 mph
exp: Unless signs say otherwise, the limit in any urban or residential district is 30 mph.

q: Under Georgia's Super Speeder law, which conviction adds a $200 state fee?
a: 85 mph or more on any road
b: 70 mph or more on any road
c: 75 mph or more on an interstate
d: 10 mph or more over the limit
exp: A conviction for 85 mph or more anywhere, or 75 mph or more on a two-lane road, brings a $200 state fee.

q: What following distance does the Georgia Drivers' Manual teach as the basic count?
b: 2 seconds
c: 4 seconds
d: 6 seconds
exp: Count one thousand one, one thousand two; if you pass the point before you finish, you are too close.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 8, Following Too Closely, p. 40

q: What is the Georgia speed limit on an unpaved county road when no sign is posted?
b: 25 mph
c: 45 mph
d: 55 mph
exp: Georgia sets 35 mph on unpaved county roads unless signs say otherwise.

q: What is the highest speed limit Georgia allows, where posted, on interstate highways?
b: 75 mph
c: 70 mph
d: 80 mph
exp: Interstates and fully access-controlled divided highways may be posted at up to 70 mph.

q: On a Georgia two-lane road, what speed triggers the Super Speeder fee?
b: 70 mph or more
c: 75 mph or more
d: 85 mph or more
exp: On two-lane roads, the Super Speeder threshold is 75 mph.

q: A Georgia driver does not pay the Super Speeder fee within 90 days of the notice. What happens?
b: Points are added, but no suspension
c: Nothing; the fee is dropped
d: The license is suspended
exp: Not paying within 90 days suspends the license, and reinstatement costs another $50.

q: According to the Georgia manual, how much following distance should you leave behind a motorcycle?
b: 1 second
c: 2 seconds
d: 8 to 10 seconds
exp: Allow three or four seconds behind a motorcycle so the rider has room to maneuver or stop.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 9, Following Too Close, p. 43

q: On a Georgia road with no sign, what is the limit outside cities on a regular two-lane highway?
b: 60 mph
c: 65 mph
d: 55 mph
exp: Where no other default applies, the Georgia limit is 55 mph.

q: What do you need to use Georgia's toll Express Lanes?
a: Cash or a card for the toll plaza
b: At least two people in the vehicle
c: A special express lane license plate
d: A registered Peach Pass in your vehicle
exp: Georgia's tolled Express Lanes require a registered Peach Pass transponder; violators get a notice by mail.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Controlled-Access Roadways, p. 23

q: What is the most a first HOV lane violation can cost in Georgia?
exp: HOV fines are up to $75 for a first offense, rising to $150 with a point on the fourth.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 8, HOV Lanes, p. 40

q: Which Georgia HOV violation also adds a point to your driving record?
b: The first offense
c: The second offense
d: None; HOV fines carry no points
exp: A fourth or later HOV violation brings a fine of up to $150 plus 1 point.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 8, HOV Lanes, p. 40; O.C.G.A. 40-5-57

q: On the I-85 Express Lanes, which carpools may ride toll-free with a registered Peach Pass?
b: Three or more people
c: Four or more people
d: None; every vehicle pays
exp: Registered carpools of three or more people use the I-85 Express Lanes toll-free.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 7, Express Lanes, p. 33

q: When may you enter Georgia's reversible I-75 Express Lanes?
a: Any time, if traffic is light
b: When the gates are closing, if you hurry
c: Only when the access gates are open
d: On weekends and holidays
exp: You may not enter the reversible Express Lanes when the gates are closed or closing.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Controlled-Access Roadways, p. 23

q: In Georgia, how close to a fire hydrant may you park?
b: No closer than 10 feet
c: No closer than 20 feet
d: No closer than 30 feet
exp: Georgia bans standing or parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, except to drop off or pick up a passenger.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Stopping, Standing and Parking, p. 20

q: In Georgia, how close to a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal may you park?
b: No closer than 30 feet
c: No closer than 20 feet
d: No closer than 50 feet
exp: You may not park within 30 feet of a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Stopping, Standing and Parking, p. 20

q: In Georgia, how close to a railroad crossing may you park?
b: No closer than 15 feet
c: No closer than 30 feet
d: No closer than 100 feet
exp: Georgia bans parking within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Stopping, Standing and Parking, p. 20

q: In Georgia, how close may you park across the street from a fire station driveway?
b: No closer than 75 feet
c: No closer than 30 feet
d: No closer than 50 feet
exp: On the opposite side of the street, the limit is 75 feet from a fire station driveway; on the same side, it is 20 feet.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Stopping, Standing and Parking, p. 20

q: In Georgia, how close to a crosswalk at an intersection may you park?
b: No closer than 15 feet
c: No closer than 30 feet
d: No closer than 20 feet
exp: Georgia bans parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Stopping, Standing and Parking, p. 20

q: Your car breaks down on a Georgia highway and you must leave it. How far should drivers be able to see it from each direction?
b: 100 feet
c: 200 feet
d: 500 feet
exp: Move off the highway if you can, and leave a clear view of the car for 200 feet each way.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, Stopping, Standing and Parking, p. 20

q: In Georgia, what is the minimum space you must leave when passing a bicycle?
b: 4 feet
c: 6 feet
d: 3 feet
exp: Georgia requires at least three feet between your vehicle and the bicycle at all times while passing.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-56; GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 9, p. 43

q: You must pass a cyclist on a Georgia road posted at 45 mph, and you cannot change lanes. How fast may you go?
b: No faster than 25 mph
c: No faster than 40 mph
d: Up to 45 mph
exp: Slow to at least 10 mph under the limit or 25 mph, whichever is higher; at 45 mph that is 35 mph.

q: What does Georgia law tell you to do first when passing a bicycle on a multi-lane road?
a: Honk so the cyclist moves onto the shoulder
b: Move to a lane not next to the cyclist
c: Pass in the same lane at least 3 feet away
d: Slow to 15 mph and follow the rider
exp: If conditions allow, make a lane change into a lane not adjacent to the bicycle.

q: What is the most you can be fined in Georgia for passing a bicycle unsafely?
exp: Violating Georgia's bicycle passing law is a misdemeanor with a fine of up to $250.

q: In Georgia, you must notify police immediately after a crash that causes injury, death, or property damage of at least how much?
exp: Georgia law requires immediate notice to police for injury, death or apparent damage of $500 or more.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-273; GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 11, p. 50

q: In Georgia, how close must an oncoming vehicle be before you switch to low beams?
b: 500 feet
c: 300 feet
d: 1,000 feet
exp: Dim your headlights when you are within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-8-31; GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, p. 24

q: It is raining lightly at noon in Georgia. Must your headlights be on?
b: If visibility is under 200 feet
c: On interstates, not city streets
d: Yes, whenever it is raining
exp: Georgia requires headlights any time it is raining.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-8-20; GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, p. 24

q: In Georgia, when you follow another vehicle, within what distance must you use low beams?
b: 200 feet
c: 500 feet
d: 1,000 feet
exp: Do not use high beams within 200 feet behind another vehicle.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-8-31; GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, p. 24

q: When must Georgia drivers have headlights on at the end of the day?
b: From an hour after sunset
c: From a half hour after sunset
d: Once the streetlights come on
exp: Headlights are required from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise.

q: In Georgia, you must use headlights when you cannot clearly see people and vehicles how far ahead?
b: 200 feet
c: 500 feet
d: 1,000 feet
exp: Headlights are required whenever visibility is not enough to see persons and vehicles 500 feet ahead.

q: After a minor crash on a Georgia multi-lane highway, no one is hurt and both cars run normally. What should you do?
a: Leave the cars exactly where they stopped for police
b: Move the cars out of traffic to a safe spot
c: Drive home and report it later
d: Wait in the cars with flashers on
exp: Georgia expects drivers to move drivable vehicles off the roadway when there is no apparent serious injury; this does not make them at fault.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 11, Moving Vehicles Following a Crash, p. 50

q: A marked Georgia police car signals you to stop, but the shoulder ahead is narrow and unsafe. What may you do?
a: Signal or use flashers and go on to a safe place
b: Stop at once on the narrow shoulder
c: Speed up to reach the next exit fast
d: Keep driving until the officer uses a siren
exp: Georgia law lets you signal or use flashers and continue at the speed limit to a reasonably safe place to stop.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-74(b), as amended by HB 1161 (eff. July 1, 2026)

q: During a Georgia traffic stop, an officer asks you to sign a ticket. What does signing mean?
a: You admit you broke the law
b: You give up your right to court
c: You agree to pay the fine today
d: It is not an admission of guilt
exp: Signing a ticket does not admit guilt, but refusing to sign can lead to arrest.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, What to Do When Pulled Over, p. 3

q: According to the Georgia manual, when should you tell an officer you have a weapon in the car?
b: After you hand over your license
c: At first contact
d: After you step out of the car
exp: Let the officer know about a weapon in the vehicle when they first approach.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, What to Do When Pulled Over, p. 3

q: You are pulled over at night in Georgia. What does the manual suggest you do with the inside light?
b: Turn it off
c: Flash it twice
d: Leave it as it is
exp: Turning on the interior light at night helps the officer see inside the car.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, What to Do When Pulled Over, p. 3

q: In fog, what does the Georgia manual say about your lights?
a: Use high beams to see farther
b: Use only parking lights
c: Turn on hazard flashers and keep driving
d: Use your low beams
exp: High beams glare back in fog; drive on low beams and do not rely on parking or hazard lights.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 8, Fog, p. 38

q: At what BAC is a Georgia driver under 21 considered under the influence of alcohol?
b: 0.00, any trace at all
c: 0.05 or more
d: 0.08 or more
exp: Under 21, a BAC of 0.02 or more is DUI in Georgia.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-6-391(k); GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, p. 23

q: What happens if you refuse a state chemical test after a Georgia DUI arrest?
a: Your license is suspended for 30 days
b: Nothing, if you are later found not guilty
c: Your license is suspended for at least one year
d: You get a warning for a first refusal
exp: Refusal brings a license suspension of at least one year, and refusing a blood or urine test can be used as evidence at trial.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-5-67.1; GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 10, Implied Consent, p. 47; Elliott v. State (Ga. Supreme Court): breath test refusal not admissible

q: You are stopped at a red light in Georgia. May you hold your phone to read a text?
a: Yes, the car is not moving
b: No, only while lawfully parked
c: Yes, if you keep your foot on the brake
d: Yes, if you are 18 or older
exp: The law allows holding a phone only when lawfully parked; a red light is not parked.

q: What is the BAC limit for an adult driver 21 or older in Georgia?
exp: A driver 21 or older is under the influence at 0.08 or more.

q: What is the BAC limit for a commercial vehicle driver in Georgia?
exp: Commercial motor vehicle drivers are under the influence at 0.04.

q: After you take the state's chemical test in Georgia, what may you request?
a: Your own extra test, at your own cost
b: A free second test by the same officer
c: Nothing; the state test is final
d: A test only after you speak to a judge
exp: You may get additional tests from qualified people you choose, at your own expense.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 10, Implied Consent, p. 47

q: What is the fine range for a first DUI conviction in Georgia?
exp: A first DUI brings a fine of $300 to $1,000 plus other penalties.

q: For a first DUI conviction in Georgia, what is the jail range set by law?
b: 6 months to 2 years
c: No jail for a first offense
d: 10 days to 12 months
exp: The law sets 10 days to 12 months; at 0.08 or more a judge may suspend all but 24 hours.

q: How many hours of community service does a first adult DUI conviction in Georgia require at minimum?
exp: A first DUI conviction requires at least 40 hours of community service.

q: For a first DUI conviction at age 21 or older, how long is a Georgia license suspended?
b: 30 days, with a limited permit
c: 6 months, with no early reinstatement option
d: 3 years, with no limited permit
exp: The suspension is 12 months; after 120 days the driver may apply for early reinstatement.

q: A passenger opens a can of beer in your car on a Georgia highway. What is true?
a: It is legal because the driver is sober
b: It is legal if the can is in a cup holder
c: It is an open container violation
d: It is illegal only at night
exp: Georgia bans drinking or possessing an open alcoholic drink in the passenger area, except for passengers in a hired vehicle or a motor home's living quarters.

q: What is the maximum fine for an open container violation in Georgia?
exp: An open container violation carries a fine of up to $200 and, for a driver, 2 points.

q: An 18 year old Georgia driver is convicted of a first DUI with a BAC of 0.05. How long is the license suspended?
b: 6 months
c: 12 months
d: 18 months
exp: Under 21, a first DUI suspends the license for 6 months, or 12 months if the BAC was 0.08 or more.

q: A 19 year old in Georgia is caught buying beer. What is the most a first conviction can bring?
b: A $300 fine and 6 months in jail
c: A $50 fine
d: A $5,000 fine and 2 years in jail
exp: Buying or possessing alcohol under 21 is a misdemeanor punishable by up to $300, up to 6 months in jail, or both.

q: What is the maximum fine for a first hands-free law conviction in Georgia?
exp: A first conviction carries a fine of up to $50 and 1 point.

q: Which phone use does Georgia's hands-free law allow while driving?
a: Using GPS navigation on a mounted phone
b: Reading a text at low speed
c: Holding the phone on speaker for a call
d: Watching a short video at a stop
exp: Navigation, voice-to-text and calls through an earpiece, watch or mount are allowed; holding the phone is not.

q: Under Georgia law, how must a child under 8 ride in a car?
a: In any seat, with a seat belt only
b: In the front seat, in a fitted booster
c: In a fitted car seat or booster, in back
d: In a car seat until 4, then a seat belt
exp: Children under 8 must ride in a proper child restraint in a rear seat, unless no rear seat is available.
src: O.C.G.A. 40-8-76; GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 5, p. 24

q: What are Georgia's minimum liability insurance amounts?
a: $15,000 per person, $30,000 per crash, $5,000 property damage
b: $25,000 per person, $50,000 per crash, $25,000 property damage
c: $50,000 per person, $100,000 per crash, $50,000 property damage
d: $10,000 per person, $20,000 per crash, $10,000 property damage
exp: Georgia requires at least 25,000 and 50,000 dollars in bodily injury coverage and 25,000 dollars in property damage coverage.
src: Georgia Office of Insurance Commissioner (oci.georgia.gov/insurance-resources/auto)

q: How many points within 24 months bring a license suspension for a Georgia driver 21 or older?
exp: Georgia suspends a license at 15 or more points in any 24 month period.

q: In Georgia, who must wear a seat belt in the back seat?
b: Every passenger of any age
c: No one; belts are needed only in front
d: Only passengers under 8
exp: Everyone in front must buckle up, and minors 8 and older must be belted in every seat.

q: A 15 year old rides unbelted in your back seat in Georgia. Who gets the ticket?
b: The 15 year old
c: The teen's parent, wherever they are
d: No one; the back seat is exempt
exp: The driver is guilty of failing to secure a minor and may be fined up to $25.

q: A child of 7 is 4 feet 10 inches tall. What does Georgia law allow?
a: The child must still use a booster
b: The child may use a regular seat belt
c: The child must ride in a rear-facing seat
d: The child may ride unbelted in back
exp: A child under 8 who is over 4 feet 9 inches tall must use a seat belt instead of a car seat.

q: What does a first child restraint violation bring in Georgia?
b: A fine of up to $500 and 4 points
c: A license suspension
d: A fine of up to $50 and 1 point
exp: The first offense carries up to $50 and 1 point; later offenses up to $100 and 2 points.

q: Which Georgia vehicles need an annual emissions test?
a: Most gas cars in 13 metro Atlanta counties
b: Every gas vehicle in the state
c: Diesel trucks in every county statewide
d: Cars over 25 years old in every county
exp: Annual emissions testing applies to gasoline cars and light trucks in 13 metro Atlanta counties; the three newest model years are exempt.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 8, Protecting the Air, p. 41

q: You move to a new address in Georgia. How soon must you update it with DDS?
b: Within 30 days
c: Within 60 days
d: At your next renewal
exp: Georgia drivers must update their address with DDS within 60 days, in person or online.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 4, Address Change, p. 15

q: How can a licensed Georgia driver reduce points on their record?
a: Pay a point reduction fee to DDS
b: Go 6 months without a new ticket
c: Retake and pass the DDS knowledge exam
d: Take a certified defensive driving class
exp: A certified 6-hour course can remove up to 7 points, once every five years.
src: GA DDS Drivers' Manual, Section 10, Points Reduction, p. 48

q: How many points does speeding 19 to 23 mph over the limit add in Georgia?
exp: Speeding 19 to 23 mph over adds 3 points.

q: Do Georgia seat belt tickets add points to your record?
b: Yes, 2 points
c: No
d: Only for drivers under 18
exp: A seat belt violation is not a moving violation for the point system.

q: Which Georgia offense adds 6 points?
b: Speeding 15 mph over
c: A first hands-free violation
d: An open container
exp: Aggressive driving, passing a stopped school bus and speeding 34 mph or more over each add 6 points.

q: What score do you need to pass the Georgia Class C or D road test?
b: 70 percent
c: 80 percent
d: 90 percent
exp: A minimum score of 75 percent is required.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: On the Georgia road test, how close to the curb must your car end up when you parallel park?
b: No more than 12 inches
c: No more than 18 inches
d: No more than 24 inches
exp: Park midway between the two standards, no more than 18 inches from the curb.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: On the Georgia road test, about how far must you back in a straight line?
b: 20 feet
c: 100 feet
d: 200 feet
exp: You back about 50 feet at no more than 10 mph, looking behind you, without crossing the boundary lines.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: During straight line backing on the Georgia road test, what must you do?
b: Watch the side mirrors closely
c: Back at about 15 mph to keep it straight
d: Turn your head and look behind the car
exp: Turn your head and look back, moving slowly and smoothly at no more than 10 mph.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)

q: Your car has lane keeping assist and a parking aid. What does Georgia require on the road test?
a: They must be removed from the car first
b: Show you can drive without those features
c: You must use them for every maneuver
d: The test must be taken in a DDS-owned car
exp: Driver assistance features are allowed, but you must show you can operate the vehicle without them.
src: DDS online manual, Section 3 Testing Information (dds.georgia.gov/book/export/html/33626)
